problems: Plant Keeper and Canvas-Jacket Neighbour share almost the same plain torso-and-sleeve silhouette. Their small handheld props carry too much of the distinction at stream scale.
The plant resembles an ice-cream cone: a pointed brown container topped by one round green scoop.
The canvas jacket has no readable opening, collar or panels; the library regular's long rectangular garment and central stripe read more like a tunic than a modern cardigan.
Both maintenance variants and the tour guide have dark head/hair geometry protruding through their hat crowns.
The maintenance vest changes from muted blue-grey to purple across wearers. Its lone low reflective stripe does not create a strong, consistent safety-workwear identity from above.

The mayor's sash is effective, but the small badge and empty rectangular ribbon prop do not provide a strong permanent symbol of office. The guide's travel props establish a visitor, but the upper-body silhouette overlaps the local sunhat regular.

Plant Keeper: the 'hoodie' can't be seen. The only hood part is a shirt:dark sphere at hips z -0.14, hidden behind the head from the front and nearly hidden from above, so the torso reads as a plain boxy sweatshirt. There is no pouch pocket, drawstrings or hood rim.
Plant Keeper: the potted plant reads as an ICE-CREAM CONE. The pot is a cone rotated pi on z, so it is a tip-down cone under a green ball. On stream it looks like someone holding a cone.
Plant Keeper: the bible calls for trainers, but the base dark shoes are untouched. The kit has no white sole and no coloured upper, which is the single strongest modern-footwear cue at this scale.

Canvas-Jacket Neighbour is the base figure plus a phone. The jacket is one shirt-coloured box exactly like the Plant Keeper's torso: no open front, no inner shirt, no collar, no pockets, no rolled cuffs. Kits 1 and 2 are indistinguishable at stream scale except for the held item and a tiny hair bun.

Canvas-Jacket Neighbour and leader: the shoes use 'pants:dark', so jeans run straight into blue boots and the person looks like they wear one-piece blue legs. Work shoes need a fixed leather or dark rubber colour.

Sunhat Library Regular: the 0.82-tall shirt-coloured box with a light vertical strip down the front reads as a long lab coat or dressing gown, not everyday modern wear. The yellow brimmed sunhat also clashes with the leader's yellow brimmed hat, so the two read as the same 'hat person'.

Town Maintenance Worker: the vest uses 'accent', so it renders grey on one person and PURPLE on the other. A hi-vis vest that isn't hi-vis loses the whole read. The reflective band is good, but there are no shoulder straps or vertical bands.

Town Maintenance Worker: the cap crown sits ON TOP of the base hair box. It renders as a stacked tall block (cap disc, then dark hair band, then the bill) like a chef hat. The bill (box at head y 0.30, z 0.18) drops over the eyes and hides half of them.
Mayor: the hair is a flat dark box 0.115 tall on top of the head. From the front and from above it reads as a short TOP HAT or fez, the exact thing the bible says not to keep from the Alderman.

Mayor: suit, trousers and shoes are all shirt:dark and render near-black. That gives an undertaker/Victorian silhouette rather than a contemporary suit. There is no visible shirt-and-tie V, and the lapels are two small light slivers.

Mayor: the 'ribbon loop' is four accent boxes forming an open gold RECTANGLE on the right hand. It reads as a picture frame or a big key, not a ribbon. The scissors (gold rings, grey blades, on the left hand) are fine, but the ribbon undermines the office read. The sash also uses 'accent', so the main symbol of office changes colour per person.

Far-Routes Tour Guide: the 'bucket hat' is two stacked cones (peaked crown plus a sloping cone brim). It reads as a conical paddy/campaign hat, which risks the stereotype the bible warns against, and it doesn't read as a bucket hat. The hair band still shows between brim and face, so the hat seems to float.

Far-Routes Tour Guide: from far away the leader is just a red-shirted resident with a yellow hat. That is the same base shape as the Plant Keeper and the same hat colour as the Sunhat Regular. Nothing rises above the head line. The 'bright practical jacket' is the plain shirt box, and the accent 'scarf' block at the neck renders as a grey yoke or harness, not a scarf.

Fit: the leader's suitcase (armR, 0.36 wide, centred -0.94) sticks out 0.1 past each side of the arm. It clips into neighbours and at ground level, and it sways with the arm as a huge slab. Acceptable as a carried roller, but it should sit tighter to the body side.

Overall modern read: kits 3 and 4 carry modern cues (sunhat, tote, hi-vis, cap, toolbox), but kits 1, 2 and the leader are 'base figure recoloured'. Nothing in their silhouette says contemporary: no hood, no sneakers, no open jacket, no earbuds or backpack.
fix:
Plant Keeper: Replace the pointed cone with a flat-bottomed terracotta cylinder and a wider rim; use two or three angular leaf clusters rather than one sphere. Add a clearly bounded gardening apron with contrasting straps and shorten the sleeves to distinguish this kit from the jacket. Seat the pot against the gripping hand. Canvas-Jacket Neighbour: Build an unmistakable waist-length jacket using a contrasting central opening, broad folded collar and two chunky front panels; keep the phone secondary rather than enlarging it into the main identifier. Sunhat Library Regular: Retain the successful broad hat and tote, but replace the central stripe with an open cardigan exposing a contrasting inner shirt. Shorten or split the lower front so the rigid hips-mounted garment cannot bridge moving thighs; attach the tote handles visibly to the hand. Town Maintenance Worker: Replace or suppress hair geometry beneath a properly fitted cap crown on both body variants. Use a fixed bright safety-yellow or orange vest over contrasting sleeves, with broad reflective shoulder strips connected to the waist band; retain the toolbox and boots. Mayor of the Civic Ribbon: Keep the dark suit and broad gold sash. Add a large, high-mounted civic medallion on a chunky chain, connect the sash over the shoulder, and replace the empty rectangular frame with a short solid ceremonial ribbon held at one end. Simplify the scissors into a clean, readable silhouette without making the event props compete with the office insignia. Far-Routes Tour Guide: Fit a rounded modern travel-hat crown over the actual head/hair bounds, removing all protrusions. Give the guide a distinct high-contrast travel vest and a short raised guide pennant, while retaining the scarf and stickered suitcase as arrival cues. Keep the suitcase outside the leg swing and its handle in the hand.
